sentences.text:
Author: Juvvadi Sridevi
Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi
 Criminal Petition No.11695 of 2024
Order :

Petitioner/accused has filed this petition under Sections 480 and 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhitha, 2023, seeking bail in S.C.No.1208 of 2018 on the file of Fast Track Special Judge for Trial and Disposal of Rape and POCSO Act Cases, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar (hereinafter referred to as 'trial Court'), registered for the offences under Sections 420, 376 (1) (a)
and 306 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012.

entities.text: Fast Track Special Judge for Trial and Disposal of Rape and POCSO Act Cases, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri G.Sundaresan, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri M.Ramachandra Reddy,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State-respondent and perused the record.
3.
The case of the prosecution is that on the false promise of marriage, the petitioner/accused has participated in sexual intercourse with the deceased several times, due to which, she became pregnant.
Thereafter, as the petitioner/accused refused JS, J to marry her, the deceased committed suicide by hanging.

Basing on the complaint dated 05.12.2016 lodged by the de facto complainant,
the Police have registered a case in Crime No.868 of 2016 against the petitioner/accused.
During the course of investigation, petitioner/accused has obtained bail and later charge sheet was filed.

The trial Court has issued non-bailable warrants against the petitioner/accused on 23.07.2024, since he failed to appear before the Court and he was remanded to judicial custody, pursuant to execution of said warrants.
4. Case of the petitioner is that his grandmother is suffering with ill-health and as he is the only person to take care of her, he could not attend before the trial Court on 23.07.2024.

On 09.08.2024,
his grandmother died.

It is further contended that as he lost his cell phone, he could not contact his counsel, as such, he could not appear before the trial Court, but there is no intention on his part for his non-appearance.

He further undertakes to appear before the trial Court on every date of hearing,
till the conclusion of trial.
JS, J 5.

The learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the application stating that non-bailable warrants were issued against the petitioner/accused multiple times i.e., on 21.04.2022, 30.06.2022,
04.07.2023, 27.03.2024 and 23.07.2024.

He further submits that the petitioner/accused is irregular in attending the Court and at present, the matter is coming up for arguments in the trial Court and if the petitioner/accused is released on bail at this stage, there is every chance of absconding.

Hence,
Shaik Sameer vs The State Of Telangana on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105025293/
1 prayed to dismiss the petition.

entities.text: Shaik Sameer vs The State Of Telangana on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Taking note of the submissions made by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, this Court is of the considered view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, this criminal petition is dismissed.
_ __ JUVVADI SRIDEVI, J Date: 04.10.2024 lk Shaik Sameer vs The State Of Telangana on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105025293/
